promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Origins and rise of independence movements

questions.q: Gandhi's philosophy of non-violent resistance is known as:
questions.explain: Satyagraha ('truth-force') underpinned Gandhi's non-violent civil disobedience in India.

questions.q: Gandhi's Salt March (1930) was a protest against:
options: The British salt tax and monopoly
questions.explain: The Salt March defied the British salt monopoly, a landmark act of civil disobedience.

questions.q: India gained independence from Britain in:
questions.explain: India became independent in 1947, accompanied by partition.

questions.q: The partition of British India in 1947 created:
questions.explain: Partition created two states, India and Pakistan, amid mass migration and violence.

questions.q: Kwame Nkrumah led which country to independence in 1957, the first sub-Saharan African colony to do so?
questions.explain: Ghana under Nkrumah became independent in 1957, inspiring wider African decolonisation.

questions.q: Ho Chi Minh led the independence struggle in:
questions.explain: Ho Chi Minh led Vietnamese nationalists against French colonial rule.

questions.q: A common cause of 20th-century independence movements was:
options: Nationalism and opposition to colonial rule
questions.explain: Rising nationalism and rejection of colonial domination drove independence movements.

questions.q: The Second World War contributed to decolonisation by:
questions.explain: War-weakened European powers found it harder to hold colonies, accelerating decolonisation.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was:
questions.explain: The INC was central to the campaign for Indian self-rule and independence.

questions.q: Algeria's independence from France (1962) is an example of a movement that involved:
questions.explain: The Algerian War (1954-62), led by the FLN, was a violent struggle for independence.

questions.q: Pan-Africanism promoted:
options: Unity and self-determination of African peoples
questions.explain: Pan-Africanism encouraged solidarity and independence across the African continent.

questions.q: A common challenge facing newly independent states was:
options: Nation-building amid economic and ethnic difficulties
An immediate absence of any problems
The return of colonial rule by choice
questions.explain: New states often faced weak economies, borders drawn by colonisers and internal divisions.

questions.q: In 1956, Egypt's leader Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised the:
questions.explain: Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal triggered the 1956 Suez Crisis.

questions.q: A leader of Kenya's path to independence was:
questions.explain: Jomo Kenyatta became a key figure and first leader of independent Kenya.

questions.q: The Amritsar Massacre (1919) helped to:
questions.explain: British troops firing on civilians at Amritsar intensified opposition to colonial rule.

questions.q: 'Negotiated independence' means independence achieved mainly through:
questions.explain: Some colonies gained independence through negotiation rather than armed struggle.

questions.q: Simon Bolivar is associated with independence struggles in:
questions.explain: Bolivar helped liberate several South American territories from Spanish rule in the 19th century.

questions.q: Majority rule and the end of apartheid in South Africa came in:
questions.explain: In 1994 South Africa held its first fully democratic elections, electing Nelson Mandela.

questions.q: Comparing Gandhi's non-violent methods with the FLN's armed struggle in Algeria is an example of:
options: Comparing the methods of different independence movements
questions.explain: Comparing and contrasting methods across cases is a key analytical skill.

questions.q: Colonial economic exploitation contributed to independence movements by:
questions.explain: Economic exploitation and inequality generated grievances that independence leaders harnessed.

specSource: IB Diploma History guide (first assessment 2020); World history topics (Paper 2): Independence movements (1800-2000)
